t: Groundskeeper at the golf course knocks off at 7 PM. The Lunker of the 7th bites at dawn and dusk. Do the math.
Every manhole in this town's got something down it. Buy a pry bar off Lou and drop a line. Three tries a hole, then let it rest.
There's a gap in the golf course fence. South side, way east, behind the bushes. Didn't hear it from me.
Something big lives under this bridge. Night only. Fish right off the side.
Old Whiskers in Maple Park Pond only feeds at night. He's taken three rods off me.
The koi pond guard walks the same square all day. Count his steps. Hide in the planters. And buy a lanyard. Nobody looks twice at a lanyard.
The storm drain past the bridge? Flashlight and waders, both. Go at night if you want to meet the Sewer King. Then let him go.
Power station's got a hole in the east fence, down in the mangroves near the bottom. Warm water, big fish, sea cows. Watch the cameras.
Bait matters. Bread for koi and carp, shrimp for anything salty, lures for bass, hot dogs for the ugly stuff. Worms for everything else.
Heron Lakes? Wait by the gate till a resident drives in and walk in right behind them. Or paddle up the back channel off the Back Canal.
Sunsplash Jungle sweeps the park at six. Nobody checks the restroom. After that it's you and the volcano.
Airport canal: when a jet comes in, everybody looks up. That's your window. There's a hole in the fence on the west side, by the bushes.
Every seventh night something glows green over the Sunsplash lagoon. I don't fish it. You might.
Plant security takes his coffee break at 2 AM. Thirty minutes, like clockwork. At night they run a floodlight off the turbine hall, so come in from the mangroves.
Don't sit in that warm water too long. My cousin started glowing in '94. Fished great. Couldn't sneak up on anything.
King tide floods Low Street every fourth day, ten to two. The Parking Lot Tarpon swims in with it.
Downtown's way south, past the airport. Two-dollar bus from Lou's. Rosa fishes the end of the Municipal Pier. She knows the bay better than I know my own feet.
Rain's the best fishing there is. Fish get brave and the guards stand under the awnings. A thunderstorm's even better, if you don't mind the lightning.
